1.word_for_word: एकादशे — in the eleventh chapter; समागत्य वृन्दावनम् — having come to Vṛndāvana; अथार्भकैः वत्सान् पालयता अनेन — then, while this one was tending the calves with the boys; हतौ वत्स-बकासुरौ — Vatsāsura and Bakāsura were slain; निर्घातः वज्र-पातः — nirghāta means the fall/strike of a thunderbolt; इति भयेन शङ्किताः — thus they were apprehensive through fear.
1.translation: In the eleventh chapter, after coming to Vṛndāvana, while this child was tending the calves with the other boys, Vatsāsura and Bakāsura were slain by Him. ‘Nirghāta’ means the strike of a thunderbolt; the cowherds were apprehensive from fear of such a portent.

2-3.word_for_word: तत् लक्ष्यं प्रत्यक्षतः पुरतः दृश्यम् अपि — that evident thing, though directly visible before them; पतन-कारणम् अविज्ञाय — not recognizing it as the cause of the fall; बभ्रमुः — they were bewildered; लक्ष्यं कारणं दर्शयति—उलूखलम् इति — he points out the evident cause with the word ‘mortar’; भ्रम-कारणम् आह — he states the cause of their bewilderment; कस्य इदं राक्षसादेः कर्म — whose deed is this, perhaps that of a Rākṣasa or the like?; कुतो वा कारणात् आश्चर्यम् उत्पातः — or from what cause is this astonishing portent?; इति कातराः भीताः सन्तः बभ्रमुः — thinking thus, distressed and frightened, they were bewildered.
2-3.translation: Although the cause was directly visible before them, they did not recognize it as the cause of the trees’ fall and were bewildered. The next verse points out the visible cause with the mention of the mortar. Śrīdhara then gives the reason for their bewilderment: they wondered, ‘Whose deed is this—perhaps that of a Rākṣasa or some other being? From what cause has this astonishing portent arisen?’ Thus, being frightened and distressed, they remained bewildered.

4.word_for_word: मध्यगेन — by Him who had gone in the middle; वृक्षयोः मध्य-गतेन — by Him who had gone between the two trees; न केवलम् एतावत् — not only this much; वृक्षाभ्यां निर्गतौ दिव्यौ पुरुषौ अपि — also the two divine persons who emerged from the trees; अचक्ष्महि — we saw; दृष्टवन्तः वयम् इति — that is, ‘we beheld them.’
4.translation: ‘By the one in the middle’ means by Him who had gone between the two trees. And it was not only this that the boys reported: ‘We also saw two divine persons emerge from the trees’; that is the meaning of ‘we saw.’

5.word_for_word: केवलं तार्किकाः — those who relied only on ordinary reasoning; न जगृहुः एव — simply did not accept it; अन्ये तु — but the others; सन्देह-युक्त-चित्ताः बभूवुः — became of minds joined with doubt.
5.translation: Those who relied only on ordinary reasoning simply did not accept what the boys said. The others, however, became doubtful in mind.

6.word_for_word: भगवन्-मायया विमोहितस्य नन्दस्य — of Nanda, bewildered by Bhagavān’s māyā; आचरितम् आह — he states the conduct; उलूखलम् इति — with the verse beginning ‘the mortar.’
6.translation: With the verse beginning ‘the mortar,’ he describes the conduct of Nanda, who was bewildered by Bhagavān’s māyā.

7.word_for_word: ‘ज्ञास्यन्ते माम्’ इति शङ्कमानः — apprehending, ‘They will recognize Me’; अतीव बाल्यम् अनुकरोति स्म — He imitated extreme childishness; तत् आह—गोपीभिः इति — this is stated with the verse beginning ‘by the gopīs’; स्तोभितः — encouraged; कर-तालादिना प्रोत्साहितः — urged on by clapping of hands and the like.
7.translation: Apprehending, ‘They may recognize Me,’ He imitated the behavior of a very small child. This is stated in the verse beginning ‘by the gopīs.’ ‘Encouraged’ means that He was urged on by their clapping of hands and similar gestures.

8.word_for_word: ‘इदम् आनय’ इति आज्ञप्तः — commanded, ‘Bring this’; आनेतुम् असमर्थ इव — as though unable to bring it; बिभर्ति केवलं पीठादि — He merely carries a stool and the like; बाहु-क्षेपं कर-चालनं च — and makes movements of the arms and hands; तद्-विदां च इति च-कार-अन्वयः — the particle ca is to be connected with ‘those who know that.’
8.translation: When commanded, ‘Bring this,’ He behaves as though unable to carry things, merely carrying a stool and the like and making movements with His arms and hands. The particle ‘ca’ is to be syntactically connected with the phrase ‘those who know that.’

9.word_for_word: तत् ऐश्वर्यं विदन्ति ये — those who know that majesty of His; तेषाम् — for them; एवं व्रजस्य हर्षम् उवाह — in this way He bore, or brought, joy to Vraja.
9.translation: ‘Those who know’ means those who know His divine majesty. In this way Bhagavān brought joy to Vraja.

21.word_for_word: रन्तुं वृन्दावनं गन्तुम् — in order to delight there, to go to Vṛndāvana; अन्तः कृष्णेन यन्त्रिताः — inwardly impelled by Kṛṣṇa; स्वतन्त्राः इव नन्दाद्याः — Nanda and the others, as though acting independently; मन्त्रम् एतम् अमन्त्रयन् — deliberated over this counsel; व्रज-कार्यं — the business of Vraja; गोकुलस्य हित-कृत्यम् — the action beneficial for Gokula.
21.translation: In order that He might sport in Vṛndāvana, Nanda and the others were inwardly impelled by Kṛṣṇa. Yet, as though acting independently, they deliberated over this plan. ‘The business of Vraja’ means what was to be done for the welfare of Gokula.

25.word_for_word: विपदं वीनाम् — the place/course of the birds; पक्षिणां पदं विहार-स्थानम् — the roaming-place of birds; विगत-प्रतिष्ठं वा — or, ‘without a firm support’; वियत् नभः — viyat means the sky.
25.translation: The expression means the roaming-place of birds; alternatively it can mean ‘without firm support.’ ‘Viyat’ means the sky.

26.word_for_word: अन्यतमो वा कश्चित् बालः — or some one of the other boys; अच्युतेन एव रक्षणम् आसीत् — protection was by Acyuta alone.
26.translation: It may refer to some one of the other boys. Their protection, however, was by Acyuta alone.

27.word_for_word: अरिष्टः — calamity; अनर्थः — misfortune; इतः स्थानात् — from this place.
27.translation: ‘Ariṣṭa’ means a calamity or misfortune; ‘from here’ means from this place.

28.word_for_word: पशव्यम् — beneficial for the cattle; पशुभ्यः हितम् — good for the animals; नवानि काननानि अवान्तराणि — fresh secondary groves; विह्यन्ते यस्मिन् तत् — that in which such groves are distributed or spread out.
28.translation: ‘Paśavyam’ means beneficial for the cattle. The place is one in which fresh subsidiary groves are spread out.

30.word_for_word: एक-धियः — of one mind; विप्रतिपत्ति-रहिताः — free from disagreement; व्रजान् — the wagon formations; शकट-व्यूहान् — arrangements of carts; रूढाः — loaded or mounted; शकटादिषु आरोपिताः परिच्छदाः यैः ते — those whose household goods had been placed upon the carts and the like.
30.translation: ‘Of one mind’ means that they were free from disagreement. ‘Vrajas’ here are formations of wagons. ‘Loaded’ describes those whose household equipment had been placed upon the carts and similar vehicles.

31-32.word_for_word: यत्ताः — prepared, intent; कृत-प्रयत्नाः — having made the necessary effort.
31-32.translation: ‘Yattāḥ’ means prepared and intent, having made the necessary effort.

33.word_for_word: नूत्नैः कुच-गतैः कुङ्कुमैः कान्तिः यासां ताः — those whose beauty came from fresh kuṅkuma upon their breasts; नूत्नेषु कुचेषु यत् कुङ्कुमम् — or, the kuṅkuma upon their youthful breasts; तेन कान्तिः यासाम् — those whose beauty was produced by that.
33.translation: The phrase describes the women whose beauty was enhanced by fresh kuṅkuma upon their breasts. Alternatively, ‘new’ may qualify the breasts themselves: their beauty came from the kuṅkuma placed upon their youthful breasts.

35.word_for_word: व्रजावासम् — the dwelling-place of Vraja; गोकुल-वसति-स्थानम् — the place of residence of Gokula.
35.translation: ‘Vrajāvāsa’ means the dwelling-place of Vraja, the place where the people of Gokula reside.

37.word_for_word: स्व-कालेन — at its own proper time; तद्-योग्य-कालेन — at the time suitable for that activity.
37.translation: ‘At its own time’ means at the time appropriate for that particular activity.

38.word_for_word: कौमार-लीलां निरूपयति — he now describes the childhood play; अविदूर इत्य्-आदिना — beginning with the verse ‘not far away.’
38.translation: Beginning with the verse ‘not far away,’ he describes their childhood play.

39.word_for_word: क्षेपणैः बिल्वामलकादि क्षिपतः — by throwing bilva fruits, āmalakas and the like; दूरे चालयतः — sending them far away; किङ्किणी-युक्तैः पादैः क्षिपतः ताडयतः — kicking and striking with feet adorned with tinkling bells; वत्स-पालाः एव द्वि-त्राः — two or three of the calf-herd boys themselves; कम्बलादि-पिहिताः — covered with blankets and the like; वृष-रूपम् अनुकुर्वन्ति — imitate the form of bulls; तैः सह स्वयम् अपि तथैव वृषायमाणौ — together with them the two boys themselves also act like bulls; नर्दन्तौ — bellowing; तद्-अनुकारि-शब्दान् कुर्वन्तौ — making sounds in imitation of them; युयुधाते — they fought.
39.translation: In their games they threw bilva fruits, āmalakas and similar objects and sent them flying far away; they kicked and struck with their ankleted feet. Two or three of the calf-herd boys would cover themselves with blankets and the like and imitate bulls. Together with them Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma likewise acted as bulls, bellowing and making sounds in imitation of them, and fought with one another.

40.word_for_word: रुतैः — by cries; शब्दैः — by sounds; जन्तून् — creatures; हंस-मयूरादीन् — swans, peacocks and the like.
40.translation: ‘With cries’ means with sounds, and ‘creatures’ refers to swans, peacocks and the like.

42.word_for_word: मुग्ध इव — as though innocent or unaware; अजानन् इव — as though not knowing; आसदत् — he approached; समीपम् आगमत् — he came near.
42.translation: ‘As though innocent’ means as though He did not know what was happening. ‘He approached’ means that He came near.

43.word_for_word: सह लाङ्गूलं यथा भवति तथा — in such a way that the tail was included; अपर-पादाभ्यां गृहीत्वा — taking hold by the two hind legs.
43.translation: He seized it by the two hind legs in such a way that the tail was held together with them.

45.word_for_word: सर्वेषां लोकानाम् एकौ मुख्यौ पालकौ — the two principal protectors of all the worlds; प्रातर्-आशः — morning meal; प्रातर्-भोज्यम् अन्नम् — food to be eaten in the morning; तत् सहितौ — supplied with that.
45.translation: They are the two chief protectors of all the worlds. ‘Prātar-āśa’ means the food eaten in the morning; the two boys were furnished with that morning meal.

49.word_for_word: राम आदिः येषां ते — those of whom Rāma was the first; न तु रामः — not Rāma himself alone.
49.translation: The expression means the group headed by Rāma, not Rāma alone.

51.word_for_word: तुण्डयोः — of the two beaks; चञ्च्वोः — of the beaks; वीरणवत् — like vīraṇa grass; अग्रन्थि-तृण-विशेषवत् — like a particular kind of grass without knots.
51.translation: ‘Tuṇḍayoḥ’ means ‘of the two beaks.’ They were like vīraṇa, a particular kind of grass without knots.

52.word_for_word: समीडिरे — they praised; तुष्टुवुः — they extolled Him; आनकैः — with drums; शङ्खैः अन्यैः च — with conches and other instruments; संस्तवैः सह — together with hymns of praise.
52.translation: ‘They praised’ means that they extolled Him, accompanied by drums, conches, other instruments, and hymns of praise.

53.word_for_word: स्व-स्थानम् आगतम् प्राणम् इव कृष्णम् — Kṛṣṇa was like life itself returned to its proper place; प्रणीय — bringing Him; एकी-कृत्य — joining Him again with them.
53.translation: Kṛṣṇa was to them like the vital breath returned to its own proper place. ‘Having brought Him’ means having reunited Him with themselves.

54.word_for_word: अतिप्रियेण — with exceedingly great affection; अतिप्रीत्या — with intense love; आदृताः — full of regard; सादराः — reverentially attentive; प्रेत्यागतम् इव — as though one had returned after death; लोकान्तरात् आगतम् इव — as though returned from another world; तृषितानि अतृप्तानि — thirsty and unsated; अमृतं पिबन्ति इव ईक्षणानि येषां ते — whose eyes seemed to drink nectar.
54.translation: ‘With exceeding affection’ means with intense love, and ‘honoring’ means receiving Him with the greatest regard. They looked upon Him as though He had returned after death, as though He had come back from another world. Their eyes were thirsty and unsated, as if they were drinking nectar.

55.word_for_word: अहो बत इत्य्-आदि-श्लोक-त्रयस्य — of the three verses beginning ‘aho bata’; इति नन्दादयः इत्य् अनेन अन्वयः — the construction is with ‘thus Nanda and the others’; अपि एवम् अपि — even so; तेषाम् एव अनिष्टम् आसीत् — misfortune befell those very beings; यतः तैः पूर्वम् अन्येषां भयं कृतम् — because previously they had caused fear to others.
55.translation: The three verses beginning with ‘aho bata’ are syntactically connected with the words ‘thus Nanda and the others.’ Even so, the calamity befell those very demons themselves, because they had formerly caused fear and harm to others.

56.word_for_word: अथ — moreover; घोर-दर्शनाः अपि — even those terrible to behold; न अभिभवन्ति — do not overpower; न घर्षयन्ति — do not assail or injure.
56.translation: Even beings terrible to behold do not overpower or injure Him.

57.word_for_word: गर्गः यत् आह — what Garga said; तस्मात् नन्दात्मजः अयं ते नारायण-समः गुणैः — ‘Therefore this son of Nanda is equal to Nārāyaṇa in qualities’; इत्य्-आदि — and so forth.
57.translation: This recalls what Garga said: ‘Therefore this son of Nanda is equal to Nārāyaṇa in qualities,’ and the rest of that statement.

59.word_for_word: वत्स-यूथ-गतः — having entered the herd of calves; हत्वा वत्स-दम्भासुरं हरिः — Hari slew the deceitful demon in the form of a calf; मुनि-यूथ-गतं च — and one who had entered the company of sages; अहन् अग्रण्यं दम्भिनां बकम् — He slew Baka, foremost of hypocrites; इति ... वत्स-बक-वधः नाम एकादशः अध्यायः — thus ends the eleventh chapter of the commentary, called ‘The Slaying of Vatsa and Baka.’
59.translation: Hari, entering the herd of calves, slew the deceitful demon who had assumed the form of a calf; and He slew Baka, foremost among hypocrites, who is compared with one who has entered a company of sages. Thus ends the eleventh chapter of the commentary on the first half of the Tenth Canto of the Śrīmad Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa, entitled ‘The Slaying of Vatsa and Baka.’
